_why: The just-ai-help config for THIS catalogue, committed. Two full 846/867-key runs in July 2026 were unreproducible because the config that drove them was never kept — the output survived in .evidence/ and nobody could say what glossary or context produced it. Run it from this directory: `node ../just-ai-help/src/translate.js just-ai-help.config.json`.
context: JustWrite, a desktop app for writing novels — chapters, scenes, a story bible of characters, locations, objects and narrative strands, and AI writing tools
_glossary: A term listed here is ALSO written into the system prompt as `never translate these terms`, so the model applies it to lowercase and inflected forms the substitution itself would never touch. That makes this list wrong for any word that must translate inside prose. Measured on the 1,965-key run: adding `AI` turned 48 CORRECT translations into findings — `Exclude from AI` -> `Excluir de la IA` is right, and shielding cannot allow it. `Strands` bled the same way, producing `la Strand narrativa` for `the narrative strand`. A word that is a label in one string and prose in another does not belong here; accept the label in es.accepted.json instead.
_strandsRemoved: "Strands" was here and came out on 2026-07-31. An English noun cannot take Spanish agreement, so every phrase using it forced the model to invent a gender — and it invented differently each time: "Strands narrativos" and "Strands narrativas" for the SAME English sentence, "strand narrativa" (masculine noun, feminine adjective), "Nueva Strands narrativa" (plural noun, singular adjective). Six variants across 47 uses. The Spanish term is now "hilo narrativo", which is already this catalogue's word for thread ("loose thread" -> "hilo suelto") and is how the English intro itself glosses a strand. If you want the feature to keep its English name in Spanish, put "Strands" back AND settle its gender by hand every run — the glossary cannot do that for you.

suspects._why: A display budget, not engine time — --escalate is what costs. At topN 30 against 150 disagreements only 20% was visible, and the two real semantic defects ranked #22 and #30 of the 30 shown, so the ranking did not earn the cut. Keep this above the disagreement count and triage the list.

_notes: engine `ollama` is the shipped default — the Gemma-4 26B-A4B QAT MoE, which carries think:false in its engine row because it is a thinking model. Switch to `ollama-gemma3` if 15 GB will not fit. MEASURED 2026-07-30 on this catalogue at 1,965 keys: 51.6 min for the full translate + BOTH --probe passes (was 21.7 min at 867 keys). Escalating the 36 flagged keys to `ollama-gemma3` afterwards cost a further 2.0 min and fixed 7 of the 8 hard defects.
